purpose: Test whether a public multilingual cross-encoder reranker can improve the frozen BGE-M3 hybrid r100 Arabic MIRACL top-100 candidate ordering.
research_basis: BGE-M3 is designed for dense, sparse, and multi-vector retrieval, so the v43 BGE-M3 hybrid r100 run is a strong first-stage candidate generator.
BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 is a multilingual reranker based on BGE-M3 and supports direct transformers sequence-classification scoring.
Qwen3/Nemotron/Jina research refresh indicates the SOTA path should combine strong first-stage retrieval, reranking, and later teacher distillation rather than further dense-only baseline chasing.

first_stage.method: Full-corpus BGE-M3 dense+sparse candidate generation followed by BGE-M3 dense+sparse+ColBERT hybrid scoring.

sample_gate_v46.decision: Scale to full dev because the same-query gate improved nDCG@10.

interpretation: BGE-reranker-v2-m3 over the frozen BGE-M3 hybrid r100 top-100 candidate pool produces a real full-dev gain: +0.016621 nDCG@10 on the same 2,896 Arabic MIRACL dev queries.
This is the strongest completed Arabic MIRACLRetrieval dev result in this repository, and it is substantially above the dense-only baselines already recorded here.
This is a retrieval-system result, not a standalone Arabic embedding checkpoint, because the final ordering uses a cross-encoder reranker over first-stage candidates.

The result is strong enough to use the reranked ordering as a better teacher signal for a trainable embedding student, while keeping public claims conservative until broader MTEB/ArabicMTEB validation is complete.
next_experiment: Run a 200-query gate with Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B over the same BGE-M3 hybrid r100 candidates, using an Arabic retrieval instruction. If it beats v47 on the same gate, scale it to full dev; otherwise use v47 as the reranker teacher for student distillation.
